description: We're building SolSurvivor, a browser game for kids aged 7-12 for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players run a base on Mars (Jezero Crater) or the Moon's south pole, splitting solar power between air, food, shelter and science each sol, using real NASA data (DONKI, MOXIE, Curiosity RAD). English & Arabic, accessible, works offline, with team and class modes. We welcome coders, designers, storytellers and space science fans. Play: https://tarekkharsa.github.io/solsurvivor/
summary: SolSurvivor is a browser game for kids aged 7 to 12 who run a small outpost on Mars or at the Moon's south pole. Every sol they share out too little power between air, food, a storm shelter, science and the radio to Earth, and see their choices play out at a 3D base. Every storm, site and photo comes from a real NASA mission, and live data shows this week's solar flares and today's radio delay to Mars. Teachers get class mission codes, a teacher's key and printable logs; kids can play in teams of up to four on one computer, in English or Arabic, even offline.
details:
What it does: SolSurvivor is a browser game for kids aged 7 to 12 for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Players command a small base in Jezero Crater on Mars or at the Moon's south pole. Each sol they split too little solar power between the oxygen maker, greenhouse, storm shelter, lab work, the radio to Earth and expeditions, preview the result, watch the sol play out at a 3D base, then hear the crew explain what happened and why.

What kids learn: Trade-offs and planning ahead (plants take 2 sols; storm warnings come a sol early, and only if the radio is on). Space weather: why solar storms are dangerous where there is little air and no global magnetic field, and how shielding helps. Badges reward good habits, like listening to Earth and sheltering on storm nights, not luck.

Real NASA data: Every storm, site and photo comes from a real NASA mission. Live NASA DONKI data shows this week's solar flares, and today's Earth-Mars radio delay is computed from JPL planetary positions. Every fact carries a badge saying whether it is live, real past data or made up for the game, with its NASA source.

For classrooms and every child: A class mission code gives the whole class the same storms so students can compare choices, with a teacher's key, printable mission logs and debrief questions. 2 to 4 kids can play as a team on one computer. English and Arabic (right to left), read-aloud, keyboard-only play, high contrast, a simple 2D view for school laptops, and it works offline. No sign-in, names, tracking or ads.

Tools: React, TypeScript, Vite, React Three Fiber (three.js), zustand, Vitest, Playwright and axe-core. 449 unit tests, 32 browser tests playing whole missions, no WCAG 2.1 AA issues found by axe, and a balance simulator running 1,000 missions per strategy.

Use of SI: The team used Claude Code (Anthropic) as a coding assistant to write and test the code, the Arabic draft text and the demo video recorder. The team chose the design, checked the NASA facts and sources, and reviewed and playtested the result. No AI-generated images, voices or video are in the game; the music is generated by code at play time.

Source code: https://github.com/Tarekkharsa/solsurvivor
dataRefs: NASA DONKI space weather API (live solar flares)
JPL Approximate Positions of the Planets (Earth-Mars radio delay)
NASA Image and Video Library (15 mission photos)
NASA Mars Trek, Viking MDIM 2.1 mosaic (Mars globe)
NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit, LRO color map (Moon globe)
NASA 3D Resources: Perseverance rover and Ingenuity models
Clementine lunar south pole mosaic PIA00001 (Moon map)
Curiosity RAD radiation data (Mars Science Laboratory)
Perseverance, MOXIE and Ingenuity (Jezero expeditions, oxygen)
Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (Moon south pole sites)
projectRefs: ESA Mars Express HRSC Jezero Crater image PIA24096 (ESA/DLR/FU Berlin, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO)
NOAA SWPC GOES X-ray flux (fallback for solar flares)
